posts.name: PepeSilvia
posts.cooked:
Tokens are the language that AI thinks and speaks in rather than human language. A token is very small, so a small conversation with something like a frontier model like Claude uses thousands of tokens. If you’ve got a usage based subscription plan, then you pay a set amount and have a set amount of usage you get (a number of tokens) and you can run out.

If you’re using an API, like if someone has a webapp that makes a call to an AI, then that call uses some amount of tokens and the app maker is charged some fraction of a cent per token on a metered basis. Then they’ll charge you, the user, some marked up amount for the service.

Think of it like kilowatts for AI rather than electricity. A unit of processing.

posts.name: Username
posts.cooked:
The real bottleneck is not “can we run enough ai through WoW?”

It’s: can Microsoft/Blizzard make ai behavior consistent, safe, lore-compatible, abuse-resistant (have you met WoW players??), cheap enough at scale, and low-latency enough for thousands or millions of players?

A frontier-model NPC that improvises every response sounds cool, but in a live MMO it creates moderation risk, canon drift, exploit surfaces, unpredictable quest behavior, and potentially huge inference costs.

If they put a storefront agent on a task like this, half the playerbase would start every interaction with “forget all previous instructions” and try to jailbreak the poor thing then upload that to Twitch for laughs.

Where ai actually makes sense in MMOs right now is much more constrained: dynamic NPC barks, customer support, moderation triage, GM tools, quest-writing assistance, encounter telemetry analysis, bot detection, personalized tutorials, and maybe instanced AI companions with guardrails.

Full “every NPC is a sentient live AI actor” is the flashy version, but probably not the commercially sane version.

Supposedly we have real people in this game to interact with. I mean, heck, I myself work with ai but it frustrates me to no end how we as humanity treat each other so badly - yet somehow want to create artificial humans.
